The Chair shall call the meeting to order at the appropriate time, greet the people, and read the
        following statement:

             •    The City of Holladay Planning Commission is a volunteer citizen board whose
                  function is to review land use plans and other special studies, make
                  recommendations to the City Council on proposed zoning map and ordinance
                  changes, and approve conditional uses and subdivisions.

             •    The Planning Commission does not initiate land use applications; rather acts on
                  applications as they are submitted. Commissioners do not meet with applicants
                  except at publicly noticed meetings.

             •    Commissioners attempt to visit each property on the agenda, where the location,
                  the nature of the neighborhood, existing structures and uses related to the
                  proposed change are noted.

             •    Decisions are based on observations, recommendations from the professional
                  planning staff, the City’s General Plan, zoning ordinance and other reports, by all
                  verbal and written comments, and by evidence submitted, all of which are part of
                  the public record.

             •    Meeting procedure can be found on the back of the agenda.
Rules of the City of Holladay Planning Commission for Public Hearings


The Planning Commission Chair or Vice Chair is the Presiding Officer and will conduct
                                    the hearing.

  1.     Introduction. The Presiding Officer informs those attending of the procedure
         and order of business for the hearing.
  2.     Staff Presentation. City Staff briefly introduces the request that prompted the
         public hearing. The presentation shall not last more than five minutes.
  3.     Sponsor Presentation. If desired, the applicant or his/her representative may
         also make a presentation. The presentation shall not last more than fifteen
         minutes.
  4.     Public Comment. The Presiding Officer asks for public comment on the
         matter before the Commission. Comments are limited to three minutes and
         speakers are allowed to speak only once. Speakers are requested to:
         (a) Complete the Citizen Comment Form
         (b) Wait until recognized before speaking
         (c) Come to the microphone and state their name and address for the record
         (d) Be brief and to the point
         (e) Not restate points made by other speakers
         (f) Address questions through the Presiding Officer
         (g) Confine remarks to the topic
         (h) Avoid personalities

         After each citizen has spoken, Commission members may ask questions of
         the participant before the Presiding Officer resumes or closes the hearing.

  5.     Applicant Summation/Response. Following citizen comment and questions
         by the Commission, the applicant shall be given an opportunity to give up to
         fifteen minutes summation and/or response prior to closing of the public
         hearing.
  6.     Closing the Hearing. If there is no further public comment, questions by
         Commission members, or final response by the applicant, the Presiding
         Officer shall conclude the hearing at least ten minutes in advance of a
         subsequently scheduled public hearing. The Commission may vote to extend
         the public hearing past the starting time of a subsequent public hearing.
  7.     Consideration of Item. At the close of the public hearing, the Commission
         shall consider the item, discuss its merits and vote on the matter or vote to
         continue it at a future meeting.

ITEM # 1
Request: Residential 2-lot Subdivision
Project: “Russell Corner Subdivision”
Address: 4585 S. Russell Street
Applicant: Mark Snow
File No.: 25-1-09
Notice: Mailed Notice on July 3, 2025
Staff: Carrie Marsh

GOVERNING ORDINANCES:
13.06           DEVELOPMENT REVIEW & APPROVAL PROCEDUREs - ADMINISTRATIVE
13.08           ADMINISTRATIVE DEVELOPMENT REVIEW STANDARDS
13.10A          SUBDIVSIONS
13.10A.070      PRELIMINARY AND FINAL SUBDIVISION REVIEW PROCESS
13.10A.080      PRELIMINARY AND FINAL SUBDIVISION APPLICATION CONTENTS

REQUIRED PLANNING COMMISSION ACTION: Administrative
Public hearing to be held. The Planning Commission shall make a motion of either denial, approval, or to
continue. All motions require findings which support the decision. As directed by ordinance, applications
shall be approved if the Land Use Authority finds Substantial Evidence of compliance with applicable
requirements. Holladay Ord. 13.06.050.B2 and 13.08

Creation of a subdivision plat requires review and approval of the preliminary plat by the Land Use
Authority (Planning Commission), as detailed in 13.10A.070.D. Decisions must be made during public
meeting.

SUMMARY
The applicant, Mark Snow, has been working with the TRC to subdivide an existing single-family parcel in
the R-1-8 zone into two separate parcels which meet the minimum lot standards of the zone. Existing
public roadways will adequately serve both lots. The subdivision will require an area to be dedicated
along Russell St. and at the corner. The subdivision will create one additional single-family parcel than
what currently exists.

BACKGROUND
Historically, Holladay was a more rural area of Salt Lake County with a lot of agricultural and orchard
land uses. These types of rural land uses were typically larger pieces of property that was subdivided
over decades. As larger properties were subdivided, there were smaller parcels retained that were not
included in formal subdivisions. Upon incorporation, Holladay maintained much of Salt Lake County’s
zoning, which dictated minimum lot standards in any given area. The R-1-8 zone has been established in



“Russell Corner Subdivision” Preliminary Review                                               Page 1 of 3
                                            City of Holladay
                                   Community and Economic Development
                                            Planning and Zoning

this area since the 1970’s.

The property has long been “super conforming”, or oversized in relation to the minimum lot standards.
Recent analysis by the applicant showed that the property could be subdivided and meet all minimum
lot standards as follows:

            Min Lot Size 8,000 sq. ft     65 ft. min lot width     48.75 ft. min. street frontage
    Lot 1           8,444 sq. ft                    yes                          yes
    Lot 2           8,005 sq. ft                    yes                          yes

Lot 1 includes a portion of land to be dedicated to the public right of way on Russell Street, a public
street to create a dedicated ROW of 50’ (25-foot half width). This lot may front on either Russell Street
or Russell Circle, to be determined at the property owner’s discretion. Lot 2 has frontage on Russell
Circle.

All utility easements are shown and a utility, grading, and other civil details have been provided. The
subdivision in not located in a sensitive lands area and does not require additional geotechnical reports.

TECHNICAL REVIEW COMMITTE ANALYSIS
In accordance with Holladay Ord 13.08.010, upon receipt of a complete subdivision application, the
Community and Economic Development Director has distributed the application to and has
subsequently received recommendation(s) from the Technical Review Committee. Review of submitted
elements are compared against the administrative checklist of required submittals 13.10.050A. The
following is provided to the Planning Commission as a summary of recommendation of preliminary
approval from the TRC:

Zoning, City Planner:
   • Lots 1 and 2 conform to 8,000 sq ft minimum lot size in the R-1-8 zone
   • Lots 1 and 2 conform to minimum lot width standards in the R-1-8 zone
   • Lots are designated as single-family in accordance with the R-1-8 zone
   • Lots 1 and 2 are both accessible by public roadways
   • Utility will serve letters have been requested/in process.
            o Utility service shouldn’t be an issue for an additional lot/dwelling unit. Water availability
                will be available by 7/14/25, power by 7/18/2025, sewer by 7/18/25 or sooner, and gas
                by 7/18/2025

United Fire Authority (UFA), Area Fire Marshal:
    • Existing access from Russell Street and Russell Circle meet fire access requirements

Engineering, City Engineer:
    • All required utility and civil details have been provided
    • Required street dedication is noted on the plat
    • Stormwater retention would be managed through building permits for each parcel

    •   Sidewalk improvements on Russell Street with ADA ramp at corner are provided

Building Code, City Building Official
    • Any building plans/improvements to either parcel would be reviewed as separate permits.

RECOMMENDATION
The TRC recommends that the commission hold the required public hearing and consider comments
presented. The CED Director has found that all required preliminary and final elements of a residential
subdivision proposal have been reviewed and accepted by the TRC and have been determined to be
substantially complete as per the City’s submission requirements. As no development is proposed at this
time (only entitlements), only a Preliminary Plat approval is required by the Planning Commission. The
TRC can recommend The Commission approve the PRELIMINARY SUBDIVISION PLAN.
In accordance with 13.10A.070.E, the FINAL PLAT approval is designated for Staff review and approval.

STAFF FINDINGS:
    1. Development details required for a Preliminary and Final plat have been submitted and
        reviewed by the TRC
    2. Each of the lots comply with the minimum width and area for single-family home development
        in the R-1-8 zone
    3. The development complies with the General Plan designation of Low Density Residential -
        Stable
    4. Fire access is existing, labeled, and approved by the UFA.
    5. Vehicular access though public roads, utility easements, and right of way improvements have
        been provided

SUGGESSTED CONDITIONS:
   1. Any outstanding utility letters to be provided prior to final approval
   2. Address any remaining comments on plat and civil plans prior to final approval

SUMMARY
Applicant, D. Rennie, representing property owner JFH Trust, has been working with the TRC on an
application for a subdivision as a Planned Unit Development. All property that is within the proposed
subdivision is owned by the same family. The family is seeking to preserve significant natural features on
the property while utilizing unclaimed density with the total area of land to enable additional family
members to build new homes that fit their individual needs on the property.

The process for a PUD involves three steps. This staff report will provide information that is relevant to
the entire project. A separate TRC review and motion will be included on individual pages for each of the
three steps detailed below. Each step will have a separate public hearing.

        STEP 1: Concept subdivision review to establish allowed number of units based on meeting
        minimum zone requirements

        STEP 2: Conditional Use Permit (CUP) review to establish the conditions associated with
        modifications to a standard subdivision for a Planned Unit Development (PUD)

        STEP 3: Preliminary subdivision review to establish and create a plat that incorporates the
        modifications made to the conceptual standard subdivision by the PUD


BACKGROUND
The Hinckley family has owned and lived on the property for over 100 years. Over time, some portions
of land have been sold to either family or other individuals. The applicant intends to keep the property
within the family, and wishes to designate specific areas where homes can be built to preserve mature
trees and other desirable features that embody the character and history of the family’s land and create
benefits to be enjoyed by residents within the development.

Currently, two parcels have existing homes and are legal, buildable lots. These two parcels are
addressed as 4880 S. Floribunda Dr. and 2830 E. Sleepy Hollow Dr. The other two parcels are related to,
or tied to, the original parcel and have not been legally approved as buildable lots. These unimproved
parcels were created with separate parcel numbers primarily for tax purposes. In order to create legal
lots, a subdivision process must occur.

PUDs are a conditional use that require a minimum area of land to qualify. The original parcel and it’s
two related parcels have enough land area to qualify for a PUD on their own, but the parcel on Sleepy
Hollow opted to be included in the PUD in order to formally establish a property line that was adjusted
previously, and in support of the perpetual preservation of consolidated open space both on their
existing parcel and within the project overall.

The proposed Planned Unit Development (PUD) involves four existing parcels totaling 1.65 acres (71,642




“Hinckley Estates” Preliminary Subdivision                                                   Page 2 of 13
                                             City of Holladay
                                 Community and Economic Development
                                             Planning and Zoning


square feet) within the R-1-10 zone. Maximum density allowances for a standard subdivision in this zone
is one unit per 10,000 square feet of land.

Density is calculated based on the net area, after required fire access is removed. In the standard
concept subdivision proposed by the applicant, the net land area results in six parcels. All six parcels are
above the minimum lot size required in the R-1-10 zone.

Minimum lot standards that are used to establish a new subdivision are:

    •   10,000 sq. ft minimum lot size
    •   80-foot minimum lot width
    •   60-foot minimum frontage width at the street

Other zoning standards for the R-1-10 zone relevant to a proposal for a PUD:

    •   20-foot front setback from a private right of way
    •   Rear setback of 22 feet (increases with lot size)
    •   Side setbacks totaling 25% of the lot width with a minimum 10% on one side (8 feet on an 80’
        wide lot), leaving 15% on the other (12 feet)
    •   Accessory building setbacks of 4 feet for lots up to 14,600 sq. ft; 5-foot setbacks for lots 14,601 –
        21,200 sq. ft.
    •   Total lot coverage of 31% for structures and 36% total – bonus would allow an increase of 10%
        toward additional hard surfaces
    •   Building height of 32 feet for lots under 15,000 sq. ft. 35 feet for lots 15,001 sq. ft to 1 acre, 40
        feet for lots over 1 acre
    •   Graduated height requires that the structure fit within a building envelope created by a 45-
        degree angle from a point that is 8 feet above the property line.

Through a Planned Unit Development, the total number of allowed units established in the conceptual
standard subdivision can be placed in desired areas within the development instead of in set lots that
are required to meet the minimum size and width of the zone. Planned Unit Developments allow
flexibility of zone standards, with the exception of unit density, building height, graduated height, and
use regulations.

The purpose of a Planned Unit Development is to:
   • Permit flexibility in land use, allow diversification in the interrelationships of various uses and
       structures with their sites and thus offer an alternative to conventional development.
   • The application of planned unit development concepts is intended to encourage unique
       neighborhoods, high quality housing, exceptional design, additional open space, and facilities
       compatible with the present living environment in the city.
   • Ensuring compliance with the purpose protects the health, safety, and public welfare of the
       future inhabitants of, or visitors to the PUD.




“Hinckley Estates” Preliminary Subdivision                                                      Page 3 of 13
                                              City of Holladay
                                   Community and Economic Development
                                              Planning and Zoning


    •   Imaginative site planning and maximizing energy utilization efficiency are significant advantages
        that can be secured through a PUD, with the objective of preserving existing greenery and
        significant trees on site.
    •   The PUD must create unique benefits for both the property owner and the city even though it
        does not allow additional density
    •   Applicants must justify why the project is better than a project developed as the underlying
        zoning would allow

The City seeks to achieve specific objectives through the flexibility of a PUD, as will be noted in the
Technical Review Committee analysis.

Along with a narrative, the applicant has provided
    1. A conceptual standard subdivision
    2. A site plan for a PUD that modifies the standard subdivision and identifies open space, tree
       protection, and establishes allowed buildable areas
    3. A civil set of plans that identifies grading, utilities (with utility will serve letters), and fire access
       details to meet the preliminary subdivision requirements

STEP 2: CONDITIONAL USE FOR A PLANNED UNIT DEVELOPMENT
TECHNICAL REVIEW COMMITTEE ANALYSIS

The TRC has verified that the applicant has submitted needed drawings and a descriptive narrative
outlining a PUD request. PUDs do not require a minimum area of land for each unit and allow for
structures to containing dwelling units to be located in areas that make sense. Lot lines within a PUD are
a personal preference as to how the applicant seeks to delineate ownership.

        Lot Size: The total land area is 71,642 square feet. The number of units allowed using the
        Maximum Density Calculation (13.04.040) is 7.
                    • Net density after removed fire access results in six dwelling units.
                    • Two dwelling units already exist on the property and two additional units are
                         being proposed. Total of 4 units proposed.
                    • All units are proposed as single dwelling units.
                              o Future desire to add dwelling units as allowed by the established
                                  density either within any identified building areas, or in new building
                                  areas, would require a modification to the PUD through the Planning
                                  Commission.

        Building Setbacks: The spacing of buildings and structures away from property lines, rights-of-
        way, physical hazards and natural features such as streams and other buildings, are essential
        elements of land use planning and of urban design. In particular, setbacks may provide for
        privacy, light, shadow, air movement, passive and active space, vegetation and also contribute
        directly to physical and psychological well-being.

        In a standard subdivision situation setback should be uniform assuming there is a specific
        desired outcome for the setback, such as privacy, public safety, economic development, etc. In a
        PUD situation, flexibility in setbacks can vary depending upon the size and shape of the
        properties, placement of structures, and the presence/preservation of existing vegetation.

        Variability and flexibility of setback may produce equally important outcomes such as the
        protection of natural features, aesthetically pleasing streetscapes, creativity in architectural
        design, and other important goals. Due to the evolution of housing styles over the last few
        decades, the relative high value of land within the community, the desire for architectural
        creativity, and especially the dramatic increase in average house construction costs, setbacks
        shall be applied within a flexible envelope.

           contribute to the character of the city;
                         • Existing homes are intended to be preserved
             4. Maximizing and preserving vegetation and open space and/or other special
           development amenities to provide light, air and privacy, to buffer abutting properties and
           to provide active and passive recreation opportunities for residents of the planned
           development and/or the community;
                         • A significant area of land that could have otherwise been legally utilized for

The addition of the proposed two dwelling units does not degrade the service level on adjacent streets

Hinckley Estates Subdivision & PUD Narrative

Address: LOT 1 - 4880 S FLORIBUNDA DR., LOT 2 - 2830 E SLEEPY HOLLOW DR., LOT 3 -
4888 S FLORIBUNDA DR.,LOT 4 - 4890 S FLORIBUNDA DR.

Holladay City Planning Commission Members,

We respectfully submit this narrative in support of a proposed residential subdivision and PUD within the
City of Holladay. The request involves four parcels. Two parcels with two existing homes and two new
proposed parcels to create two new single family homes. The intent is to preserve and protect some
mature trees and greenery and to maintain the character of the surrounding neighborhood while making
efficient and responsible use of the property.

Project Overview: The subdivision is located in R-1-10. With typical subdivision, our greenery and some
main mature trees will need to be removed. Due to the one of the lot being on the inside. Private roads
will need to be added. For a home to be built on the inside lot, it will also require removing most trees and
vegetation. We are proposing this subdivision in conjunction with PUD so we could provide an essential
protection for existing greenery and significant trees on site. PUD also provided us with more flexibility to
build two residential homes on both new proposed parcels. The homes will be owner-occupied and built
with consideration of the scale and aesthetics of the surrounding neighborhood.

Traffic Impacts: The addition of two single-family homes is not expected to result in any significant
increase in traffic volume or congestion. Vehicular access will be provided via Floribunda Drive. For fire
access purposes we are proposing 60-FOOT “Y”

Improved Quality of Life: PUD will help us be able to protect necessary greenery, decrease impervious
space and create more flexible buildable areas with greenspace effort. With the current landscape, new
landscape and preserved greenery within the subdivision will contribute to improve air quality, reduce
noise pollution and preserve some natural habitats

Compliance with Conditional Use Standards: With our best understanding, we believe this project
meets the standards outlined in Holladay City Ordinance 13.08.040F. The use will not be detrimental to
the health, safety, or general welfare of persons residing or working in the vicinity. The project involves
low-density residential use that aligns with the surrounding properties and will not introduce any unusual
or incompatible impacts to the neighborhood. No nuisances, hazards, or disruptions are anticipated. The
subdivision supports the goals of responsible residential development and neighborhood preservation

We appreciate your consideration of this request and welcome the opportunity to discuss the proposal
further. We are committed to a collaborative process and look forward to working with staff and the
Commission to ensure the best outcome for the neighborhood and the City of Holladay.

Sincerely,

Duangkamon Rennie

April 28th at 5:00 PM at Paul & Jeanie’s Home (2830 E Sleepy Hollow Drive, Holladay, UT 84117)



Name                                Address                        Signature




Meeting Minutes:
Hinckley Estates Subdivision & PUD Neighborhood Meeting - 04/28/2025

Topic to discuss for Neighborhood meeting
   ●​   Introduce who we are, this has been a family lots for over 100 years
   ●​   Reason for meeting, letting neighbors know we are proposing two new single homes on lot 4888 and 4890.
   ●​   Reason for proposing this subdivision with PUD: Preserve mature trees and make sure both lots are
        buildable. What is PUD? Planned Unit Development help with more flexibility to adapt to lot shape and size.
   ●​   Total site is 71,642 sf or 1.65 acre. Density lots allowed 7 totals so with 2 existing we can fit 5 more homes
        on those lots if we would like to turn it into a townhome. But we want to keep this as a quiet residential area.
   ●​   Questions


Meeting minutes:
  ●​ Opened the meeting introducing the buyers and the seller at 5:10pm
  ●​ Discussed the history of the land and how it has been in the family for 90 years. We are
      continuing to keep it in the family with this purchase and proposed PUD. Keeping the
      property in the family was the goal of the seller, Jean Hinckley.
  ●​ Discussed the current property lines (north/south) and the complications with those lots
      to build on.
          ○​ Land locked lot is currently not a buildable lot
          ○​ Additional road needed and can add complication to utility
  ●​ Shifted to the new proposed lines running east/west for easier road access and ability to
      build houses on those lots
  ●​ Focused on only one residential home being built on each lot
  ●​ There were a number of questions regarding why a PUD and concerns with a PUD
          ○​ Confusion over the difference between PUD and HOA’s
          ○​ Questions about why we are doing a PUD
          ○​ Discussion on the size of homes that can be built and the setback to other
              properties
          ○​ The impact of PUD and the size of it, 4 properties are included.

   ●​ There was concern from the owner of the house on the south side of the 2 lots (Ms.
      Cindy Gubler) specifically around the setback of the house and concerns that the PUD
      will allow a home to be built too close to her property line. She mentioned she was going
      to pushback on the city for this, even though we explained there are still guidelines we
      need to follow when building
   ●​ Conversation changed to the right of way and easement of Floribunda Drive since it is a
      private road and there isn’t a consensus between the neighbors on who has right of way.
      We will need to walk through this as neighbors. There was little concern over the PUD
      with these neighbors but more focused on the road.
           ○​ At this point people started to leave the meeting, around 6pm.
   ●​ Overall the neighbors were supportive of the PUD with the exception of Ms. Gubler and
      her concern of the setback of the home.
   ●​ There were 20-25 people in attendance.

                      PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
                                                  July 15th 2025

ITEM # 5
Request: Preliminary Commercial Site Plan and Subdivision Amendment within Royal Holladay Hills
Project: “Royal Holladay Hills Block C lot 2a”
Address: 1888 East Rodeo Walk Drive – Block C
Applicant: Denise Knoblich, Applicant and Steve Petersen, Owner
File No.: 19-9-19-9
Notice: Mailed Notice on July 3rd 2025
Staff: Jonathan Teerlink, CED Director

GOVERNING ORDINANCES:
13.65.070(C)                        REGIONAL MIXED-USE ZONE (RM-U)
13.03                               SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS
13.06                               ADMINISTRATIVE & DEVELOPMENT REVIEW PROCEDURES
13.08.050                           SITE PLAN
SDMP,2007                           SITE DEVELOPMENT MASTER PLAN (SDMP)


REQUIRED PLANNING COMMISSION ACTION: Administrative
Public hearing to be held PC shall make an administrative motion of either, denial, approval or to continue. All
motions require findings which support the decision. As directed by ordinance, applications shall be approved if
the Land Use Authority finds Substantial Evidence of compliance with applicable requirements. Holladay Ord.
13.06.050.B2 and 13.08

Creation of a development site plan requires review and approval by the Land Use Authority (Planning
Commission) in a two-step process; Preliminary and Final plans. Decisions must be made during public meeting.
The notice for the required public hearing of this first step has been mailed to all properties within 500’ of the
subject parcel.

SUMMARY
According to the approved subdivision plan for all Royal Holladay Hills, applicant, Steve Peterson
proposes commercial development for .33 acres (14,300 sqft) or ~20% of total area of Block “C”. Mr.
Peterson and design representatives for “Roth Living” will present a site layout and development plans
for consideration and review against the 2007 Site Development Master Plan (SDMP). Review is subject
to the provisions of the, “Open” Land Use District (O Zone). The O Zone is to be considered the most
intense land use zone within this master planned development, offering a widest range of allowed uses
and the tallest building heights (90 feet). In this case, the entire 3.5 acres is to be secured by a single-use
commercial building, intended to be occupied by Roth Living.




“RHH Block C Lot 2a” Preliminary Review                                                                 Page 1 of 2
                                                    City of Holladay
                                       Community and Economic Development
                                                    Planning and Zoning

TECHNICAL REVIEW COMMITTE ANALYSIS
PRELIMINARY PLAT DEVELOPMENT
The TRC is satisfied that the land use elements (zone compliance) of a preliminary site development plan proposed
for a portion of Block C provide all information needed for review of the Planning Commission. TRC recommends
that the following items be highlighted by the PC as they are found to be critical elements required for SDMP
compliance

    •    Commercial Retail is an allowed Permitted land use within O Zone, see page 3 of the SDMP.
    •    Access to site is to be provided internally via a new section of Royce Drive a private street.
    •    Commercial intensity (maximum square footage) is considered to be dispersed across entire site (57 acres),
         see page 1 of the SDMP.
    •    Parking is required at 1 stall per 200 square feet. This site provides 62 stalls (55 required), see page 8 of the
         SDMP
    •    Landscaping plans are provided and propose 23+ new trees and various landscaping features around the
         site.
    •    Building height is proposed at 25 feet (90 feet allowed), page 6 of the SDMP
    •    Architectural design is an element regulated by SDMP. Chosen commercial designs should be found to
         comply with the design palette on page 16 of the SDMP.

As ownership will be created, an amendment to approved subdivision plat for Block C is proposed. The
amendment is limited in scope to the creation of Lot 2a, enabling development of this site plan. The TRC
has found no other substantive changes that would prevent a Planning Commission review.

RECOMMENDATION
The required submittals for preliminary site development plan and subdivision plat for Block C are found by the
TRC to be complete as per the City’s submission standards, R-M/U zone regulations and SDMP site development
standards. The TRC recommends the Planning Commission to hold the required public hearing and moderate a
discussion with the applicants on the details of the development plan. The TRC feels the application may be
approved and strongly requests that potential PC decisions be accompanied with findings. Additionally, the TRC
can recommend that the PC delegate FINAL approvals to staff as per §13.10a of the Holladay code.

SUGGESTION MOTIONS
 “I motion to (approve_deny_continue) the PRELIMINARY COMMERCIAL SITE DEVELOPMENT PLAN and AMENDMENT TO THE
SUBDIVISON PLAT FOR BLOCK C enabling the development of “Royal Holladay Hills, Block C lot 2a” in the R-M/U zone located
at 4833 South Sunset Blvd Lane with FINAL SITE PLAN & PLAT approvals to be delegated to staff. Motion is based on the
following findings;
     1) Proposed land use of commercial retail use is an allowed permitted use.
     2) Access, site details and construction elements and details are found to be acceptable by divisions the Technical Review
          Committee
     3) All development details and all related components comply with the R-M/U zone & SDMP as a master planned project
     4) The subdivision plat amendment

Conditions for Final Approval – to be submitted to and verified/approved by Community and Economic Development Director
with a recommendation by the TRC
     1) Work with city engineering on any clarifications to submitted storm water drainage report
     2) Applicant to work with staff on all needful clarifications, if any, made by the commission during this meeting.

                     PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
                                             July 15th, 2025

ITEM # 6
Request: Ordinance Amendment
Project: Amendment to Parking and Signage location requirements of the Site Development Master Plan
(SDMP 2007) Royal Holladay Hills
Address: 5870 S. Highland Drive
Applicant: Steve Petersen, KMW Development
File No.: 07-7-01-2
Notice: Posted Class A Notice on July 2nd 2025
Staff: Jonathan Teerlink

GOVERNING ORDINANCES:
13.07.030       ORDINANCE AMENDMENT – PROCEDURE & REQUIREMENTS
13.65.080       AMENDMENTS TO SITE DEVELOPMENT MASTER PLAN

REQUIRED PLANNING COMMISSION ACTION: Legislative
Public hearing to be held. Ordinance amendments, are proposed changes to the City of Holladay Code.
Amendments can be in the form of a new standard, or an alteration to an existing rule or
regulations/standards. Decisions on proposals to amend a city ordinance is a legislative action, requiring
the Planning Commission to hold a public hearing, review the proposal and forward a recommendation,
with findings, to the City Council for final decision/action.

SUMMARY
Property owner and applicant, Steve Petersen (Applicant), proposes to clarify and update surface and
terraced parking areas designated within the site and project signage locations at the perimeter of the
site.

REQUEST
The Royal Holladay Hills redevelopment site, currently in the R/MU zone, is subject development details
provided in the 2007 Site Development Master Plan (SDMP). Sections of the SDMP are designated to
provide guidance on the location and number of on-site parking stalls provided for the project and the
project signage locations. Since the adoption of the 2007 SDMP, the Applicant has refined how to build
these elements and proposes to clarify the SDMP accordingly.

The Applicant is proposing to clarify the following pages as they relate to conceptual uses of the project
ares for parking. Primarily, to address refined plans for parking terrace on blocks “J” and “I” and refining
(i.e. reducing) the large area designated as exclusive surface parking on block “A”.
         3; Permitted Land Uses By District and Building Function
         5; Land Use Regulation Plan – Uses by Story



SDMP AMENDMENT – PARKING SIGNAGE                                                                Page 1 of 3
                                            City of Holladay
                                 Community and Economic Development
                                            Planning and Zoning

        8; Site Parking Plan
The Applicant is also refining the following pages to refine the location of an additional project
Arrival/Monument sign.
        17; Conceptual Site Lighting & Signage Plan

REASONING & PURPOSE
The overall intent of this amendment is to clarify ambiguity and interpretation some of the land use pages
as they relate to parking. Addressing parking, the amendment refines the operational location of each
area by refining the number of stalls and mass of the compact terraced parking structure and “vastness”
of the surface parking lot at the prominent corner of the project site. Additionally, the option to locate an
Arrival/Monument sign at the Murray Holladay Road entrance has been missing from the master plan
since adoption. This amendment proposed to address this missing location.

NON-CONFORMING USES
This amendment would not create any non-conforming use situations and does not alter the original
intent of the SDMP to provide adequate parking or project signage.

CONSIDERATION STANDARDS
13.07.030G: Approval Standards:
       1. A decision to amend the text of this title or the zoning map is a matter within the legislative
           discretion of the city council. The city council, after reviewing the planning commission
           recommendation, may:
               a. Adopt the amendment as recommended by the planning commission;
               b. Make any revisions to the proposed amendment that it considers appropriate;
               c. Remand the proposed amendment back to the planning commission for further
                    consideration; or
               d. Reject the proposed amendment.
       2. In reviewing a text or map amendment, the following factors should be considered:
               a. Whether the proposed amendment is consistent with goals, objectives and policies
                    of the city's general plan;
               b. Whether the proposed amendment is harmonious with the overall character of
                    existing development in the vicinity of the subject property;
               c. The extent to which the proposed amendment may adversely affect abutting
                    properties; and
               d. The adequacy of facilities and services intended to serve the subject property, such
                    as, roadways, parks and recreation facilities, police and fire protection, schools,
                    stormwater drainage systems, environmental hazard mitigation measures, water
                    supply, and wastewater and refuse collection.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff finds the proposal to be acceptable in its scope as a needful clarification and update to these
specific areas of the SDMP. Staff can therefore recommend that the Planning Commission forward a
positive recommendation to the City Council to amend pages 3, 5, 8 and 17 of the 2007 Site




SDMP AMENDMENT – PARKING SIGNAGE                                                                 Page 2 of 3
                                          City of Holladay
                                Community and Economic Development
                                           Planning and Zoning

Development Master Plan for redevelopment within the R/MU zone, as shown in Exhibit “A,” based on
the following findings:

        1. The proposal maintains regulatory intent and purpose of the Land Development Code,
           R/MU zone and SDMP.
        2. The proposal clarifys parking and signage locations within the Royal Holladay Hills
           redevelopment site and is found to not amend or alter other land use locations, provisions
           that are required or otherwise regulated in the site development master plan.
        3. The amendments maintain compliance with the Goals and Policies of the General Plan by
           establishing appropriate redevelopment standards for requiring on-site parking and
           providing commercial properties appropriate signage.

uses designated for surface and terraced parking and Arrival/Monument Sign locations, based upon
the following findings”.

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Holladay Planning Commission will hold a public hearing
on Tuesday, the 15th day of July 2025 as close to 6:00 P.M. as possible, in the Holladay City
Council Chambers, 4580 S 2300 E, Holladay, Utah.

The purpose of the hearing is to consider a proposed text amendment to the Site Development
Master Plan for the Royal Holladay Hills Redevelopment area (aka Cottonwood Mall
Redevelopment Area, 2007) within the Regional Mixed-Use zone (R/M-U). The proposal,
brought by the applicant, Steve Petersen intends to update and clarify surface and terraced
parking areas within the site and project signage locations at the perimeter of the site. Proceedings
held in accordance with Holladay Ordinance §13.07.030.

Information regarding this matter is available for public inspection on the City’s website
www.holladayut.gov and may be examined during regular business hours at the Holladay City
offices, 4580 S 2300 E, Holladay, Utah, 84117.

                       PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
                                                  July 15th 2025

ITEM # 7
Request: Site Plan Amendment
Project: “Royal Holladay Hills Block K”
Address: 4833 South Sunset Drive – Block K
Applicant: Steve Peterson, Holladay Hills, LLC
File No.: 19-9-19-6
Notice: N/A
Staff: Jonathan Teerlink, CED Director

GOVERNING ORDINANCES:
13.65.070(C)                      REGIONAL MIXED-USE ZONE (RM-U)
13.03                             SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS
13.06                             ADMINISTRATIVE & DEVELOPMENT REVIEW PROCEDURES
13.08.050                         SITE PLAN
SDMP,2007                         SITE DEVELOPMENT MASTER PLAN (SDMP)


REQUIRED PLANNING COMMISSION ACTION: Administrative
PC shall make a motion of either, denial, approval or to continue. All motions require findings which support
the decision. As directed by ordinance, applications shall be approved if the Land Use Authority finds
substantial evidence of compliance with applicable requirements. Holladay Ord. 13.06.050.B2 and 13.08

SUMMARY
Applicant Steve Peterson proposes an amendment to approved site development plans for “Block K” a
6.87-acre area located at the easternmost of the Royal Holladay Hills project area. Planning Commission
approved a preliminary development plan and architectural design for 28 detached, single family homes
and 4-story, multi-family building making up 72 units. The applicant is requesting commission approval to
change the multi-family “flats” to a townhome product and review a revised architectural design for the
new townhomes. The change in residential product will reduce the total number of units from 100 to 93.

TECHNICAL REVIEW COMMITTE ANALYSIS
The amended development plan generally follows the previously approved layout. Very minor changes to driveway
access points are result of the new townhome design, rather than a multi-unit complex.

Detached Single Family home
The 19 single family lots will be serviced via the existing utility systems located within the Royal Holladay Hills
Development. Applications for construction review of each of these homes will take place individually, based upon
review of approved design/ architectural standards as set by the SDMP. Specific setback requirements are requested as
shown in submitted civil drawings.

                                       Community and Economic Development

            The phase complies with land uses of the “Restricted” land use district – Detached Single Family
             Residential. which complies with the 13.65, RM-U Zone, and pages 1 and 3, “Permitted Land Uses by
             District and Building Functions”, of the SDMP.
            The site plans comply with the landscaping (pg 14 and 15), street cross sections (pg 11), access and
             architectural design components (pg 16).
            Site drainage comply with the master site drainage plan – see Royal Holladay Hills Subdivision #2
            Utility connection letters for the overall site are on file. These service agreements are intended to include
             this phase
            Unified Fire Authority has approved all emergency access drives.

76 Townhomes
All the townhomes have addresses on Sunset Drive. These units are proposed to be connected from the Holladay Hills
utility system. The design of all buildings are similar in styling with a maximum height of 60’ feet (Limited Use District).
Each of the building are serviced by a common parking court featuring individual garages and additional guest parking
at the peripheries.
           The land use, parking and building heights for this block comply with use regulations of page 1 and 3,
              “Limited District” and page 6, “Building Massing and Heights Plan” of the SDMP
           The site plans comply with the landscaping (pg 14 and 15), street cross sections (pg 11), access and
              architectural design components (pg 16).
           Site drainage comply with the master site drainage plan – see Royal Holladay Hills Subdivision #2
           Utility connection letters for the overall site are on file. These service agreements are intended to include
              this phase
           Unified Fire Authority has approved all emergency access drives.

RECOMMENDATION
The amendments to the site plan and architectural design of Block K are found by the TRC to be complete
as per the City’s submission standards, R-M/U zone regulations and SDMP site development standards. The
TRC can recommend the planning commission approved the amendments as proposed

Suggestion motions

 “I motion to approve the AMENDED PRELIMINARY SITE DEVELOPMENT PLAN AND BUILDING DESIGN for
“Royal Holladay Hills, Block K” a 93-unit residential subdivision in the R-M/U zone located at 4833 South
Sunset Blvd Lane with FINAL SITE PLAN & PLAT approvals to be delegated to staff, finding that the proposal;
     1) complies with the Preliminary site plan approved by the Commission for Block K,
     2) construction elements and details are found to be acceptable according to page 16 of the SDMP
         (2007) by divisions the Technical Review Committee
     3) development details and all related components comply with the R-M/U zone & SDMP as a master
         planned project

Conditions for Final Approval – within one year, according to Holladay Ord §13.10a final civil development
drawings shall be submitted to and verified/approved by Community and Economic Development Director
   1) Work with city engineering department to finalize all civil development details
   2) Work with staff on all needful clarifications, grammatical and/or formatting changes to the final
        plat prior to recording approval
   3) Submittal of a vertical ownership component to the final plat showing separation and delineation of
        owned spaces within each building; i.e common vs private

 4                               PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

12   ATTENDANCE:
13
14   Planning Commission Members:                           City Staff:
15   Dennis Roach, Chair                                    Carrie Marsh, City Planner
16   Karianne Prince                                        Jonathan Teerlink, Community and Economic
17   Jill Fonte                                                    Development Director
18   Paul Cunningham                                        Brad Christopherson, City Attorney
19
20   WORK SESSION
21   Chair Dennis Roach called the Work Session to order at 5:38 p.m. He made note of those present at
22   the Planning Commission Meeting and reported that there are three items on the Regular Meeting
23   agenda. The Commission first discussed the three sets of Meeting Minutes that will be voted on. It
24   was determined that Commissioner Paul Cunningham will make the motion for the Meeting Minutes.
25
26   The Public Hearing item on the Regular Meeting agenda is a Site Plan Amendment for 5025 South
27   Highland Drive. There is also a Continued Hearing Item for the Text Amendment for Chapter 13.84
28   – Outdoor Lighting Standards. City Planner, Carrie Marsh, discussed the Site Plan Amendment. She
29   explained that this is the site at the corner of Arbor Lane and Highland Drive. It is a Mixed-Use
30   Commercial/Residential. The previous iteration had a larger building on the corner toward the front
31   of Arbor Lane, but this iteration is pushing that building closer to Highland Drive and the intersection
32   of Arbor Lane and Highland Drive. The previous plan had residential units on the upper floor, but
33   the proposal is to remove those residential units from the upper floor and have that be a solely
34   commercial building. The proposal is to add another row of townhomes next to the previously
35   approved units. The Planned Unit Development (“PUD”) setbacks were discussed at the last Planning
36   Commission Meeting. The proposal is to maintain the same 10-foot setback on the side. As for the
37   building next to the sidewalk, there is a clear view triangle labeled. The building is outside of that
38   area for visibility. The vacation area that is referenced in the Staff Report was highlighted. The
39   motion will include a recommendation to the City Council to vacate that portion of Arbor Lane.
40
41   Ms. Marsh reviewed the square footage for the building area with the commercial space and the
42   dwelling units. The total impervious coverage and landscaped area information is included in the
43   Staff Report as well. One reason for the proposed changes to the site had to do with the fact that the
44   original commercial building had too much square footage. This puts two levels of commercial space
45   above a restaurant use. There is a stacked design and the restaurant would be on the main floor and
46   there would be two levels of office space. Parking was another reason for some of the proposed

     City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting – 04/15/2025

                                                        1
 1   changes. With a larger restaurant, there were challenges associated with a smaller parking lot. The
 2   overhead power lines are also an issue to work around. That is the reason the building was moved
 3   over instead of remaining in the previous location. She offered to answer Commissioner questions.
 4
 5   Commissioner Cunningham asked if there is a guarantee for the restaurant tenant. Ms. Marsh reported
 6   that there is a Development Agreement for a brewery restaurant. If the restaurant is not able to move
 7   ahead, then the zoning would revert to Neighborhood Commercial. The applicant has kept the
 8   restaurant use there to maintain the Development Agreement for the use on the site.
 9
10   Chair Roach noted that the Technical Review Committee (“TRC”) report recommends Preliminary
11   Subdivision approval. Ms. Marsh explained that it looked at this as a shift in units. There is still a
12   decent amount of commercial space, even though there is not the same square footage as before.
13   Chair Roach asked whether it was possible to approve something right against the sidewalk. Ms.
14   Marsh reported that there is a recommendation from Staff to move that 10 feet from Highland Drive
15   so there is a setback from the sidewalk. The Site Plan shows a 10-foot sidewalk that is required for
16   the Highland Drive right-of-way. While there is a wide sidewalk, having landscaping between the
17   sidewalk and the building is the Staff's recommendation so there is not a wall right next to the
18   sidewalk.
19
20   Commissioner Jill Fonte believed the proposal was to decrease the amount of commercial and
21   increase the amount of residential. This was confirmed. Ms. Marsh explained that the proposal is to
22   have fewer units, but a higher total square footage. Discussions were had about heights in the C-2
23   Zone and possible future redevelopment in the C-2 Zone. Chair Roach asked whether there is
24   graduated height on the building abutting Highland Drive or if it will be a three-story wall with
25   landscaped space between the building and the sidewalk. Ms. Marsh reported that there is not a
26   graduated height requirement next to roadways. That requirement applies when it is next to a
27   residential use.
28
29   Commissioner Fonte asked if there was any basis to deny the application. Chair Roach explained that
30   the Planning Commission can discuss those kinds of decisions during the Regular Meeting. At that
31   time, the applicant can also explain the reason for the proposed changes. He is interested to hear what
32   public comments might be shared during the meeting. No written comments have been submitted.
33
34   Chair Roach expressed concerns about the landscaping. In the Staff Report, it states that the Tree
35   Canopy Protection Plan is in progress. He believes there will be limited landscape options based on
36   the available land. There are power lines to take into consideration as well as the condensed area.
37   Ms. Marsh noted that the site is challenging because of the power lines, so the best location for parking
38   is in that area. However, that limits where buildings can be located on the applicant site.
39
40   Community and Economic Development Director, Jonathan Teerlink, stated that there is interest in
41   separating the uses out. Chair Roach pointed out that if the Planning Commission feels there is more
42   that needs to be presented for this application, there is the option to continue the item and receive
43   additional feedback. Ms. Marsh believes the applicant would be willing to receive feedback. In
44   addition, the public comments shared during the hearing can also provide meaningful guidance.
45


     City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting – 04/15/2025

                                                        2
 1   The Continued Hearing Item is for the Text Amendment for Chapter 13.84 – Outdoor Lighting
 2   Standards. Chair Roach stated that this might be an item to continue based on the number of
 3   Commissioners present at the meeting. The City Council would likely prefer that the full Planning
 4   Commission vote on the Text Amendments. The Staff Report was reviewed. Mr. Teerlink noted that
 5   some elements of the Purpose Statement did not sit well with the Commission, so those were removed.
 6   Some applicability standards were clarified and a clarifying definition was added for light trespass.
 7   The maximum light output for lumens was removed. Most of the amendments took place in the R-1
 8   and R-2 Zones section. The color spectrum was removed as well as the lumen maximums. There
 9   was also some reordering done to the items in that section.
10
11   Commissioner Cunningham pointed out that there is still a numbering issue. He asked that the
12   numbering be further refined. He also noted that a duplex should be referenced in the language as
13   well as single-family. Commissioner Cunningham expressed appreciation for the work that has been
14   done on the Text Amendments so far. Chair Roach noted that there could be a more detailed
15   discussion about this item during the Regular Session. It seems that there will likely be a continuation.
16
17   CONVENE REGULAR MEETING – Public Welcome and Opening Statement by Commission
18   Chair.
19   Chair Roach called the Regular Meeting to order at approximately 6:00 p.m. He noted that
20   Commissioner Angela Gong, Commissioner Ginger Vilchinsky, and Commissioner Brian Berndt are
21   all excused, but there is still a quorum present. There are three items on the Regular Meeting agenda.
22   Commissioner Cunningham read the Opening Statement for the benefit of those present.
23
24   PUBLIC HEARING
25   1.      Site Plan Amendment - 5025 South Highland Drive - Subdivision and Mixed-Use PUD
26           Amendments - 5025 South Highland Drive (C-2 Zone). Review and Consideration of
27           Amendments to Preliminary Site Approvals as Proposed by Applicant, Bret Laughlin as
28           Owner, for a Mixed-Use Residential/Retail Planned Unit Development in the C-2 Zone.
29           File #23-2-03.
30   Ms. Marsh presented the Staff Report and explained that the item was a Site Plan Amendment for
31   property located at 5025 South Highland Drive. She noted that this is a project that the Planning
32   Commission has seen a few times in the past. This property is zoned C-2 and there is a Development
33   Agreement for a brewpub restaurant and townhome. The Planning Commission previously approved
34   the Site Plan. In 2024, a revised Site Plan was approved that had the commercial building with some
35   residential units on the top floor and the original townhomes. There are now some modifications
36   proposed to the Site Plan and that is what will be considered by the Planning Commission.
37
38   The commercial building is still on the west and north end of the site, but it has been pushed closer
39   to Highland Drive than the original location. The units that were on the top floor of the commercial
40   building were removed. There were six units there before and those have been moved over as
41   additional townhome units. The property is 1.08 acres. There is a portion of the property on the east
42   and north side that is the former alignment of Arbor Lane. That portion requires a right-of-way
43   vacation, which would then become part of the property. Part of the application is a recommendation
44   to the City Council to vacate a portion of Arbor Lane. The previous Site Plan that was approved had
45   a 10-foot setback for the townhomes. The applicant has proposed to keep the 10-foot setback for
46   those townhomes. As part of that approval, the Commission stated that there needed to be more than

     City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting – 04/15/2025

                                                        3
 1   the required number of trees on the east side of the property, which is the rear of Units 1, 2, 3, and 4.
 2   The trees are not shown in the plan, so that has been referenced in the Conditions of Approval.
 3
 4   In the Staff Report, there are details about the square footage for each of the uses. There is a total
 5   tabulation of 9,800 square feet for commercial use. The footprint of each residential unit is 1,300
 6   square feet. That meets all of the requirements of the C-2 Zone. Ms. Marsh explained that one of the
 7   main points of discussion the Commission can have with the applicant is whether this meets the
 8   requirement for the residential use to be an accessory use to the commercial building. As for the
 9   landscaping, that would be a condition that needs to be shown on the final plan. Alternatively, the
10   Commission can choose to have this come back with more detailed information. Ms. Marsh added
11   that the parking design would need to meet the requirements mentioned in the Staff Report. Building
12   height was discussed. There is 40 feet of height in the C-2 Zone and there are graduated height
13   requirements next to residential property lines. Staff recommends moving the commercial building
14   10 feet from the property line so it is further away from the sidewalk. That is an area where
15   landscaping could be added to break up the appearance of the wall in that location. Chair Roach
16   believed that the graduated height would impact Units 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, which was confirmed.
17
18   The applicant, Bret Laughlin, explained that he is not a professional developer. He is a neighbor who
19   saw the dilapidated property and wanted to turn it into something special. It did not make sense to
20   have residential above the restaurant, because it was too difficult to engineer and design. There were
21   also some difficulties with parking. He is now asking to take those six residential units and build four
22   additional townhomes. It is a better use of the lane that is created and separates the residential from
23   the commercial. This will alleviate a lot of the parking issues. He believes a lot of the problems
24   associated with the residential units had to do with residential facing a restaurant parking lot. For this
25   property to make sense financially, there has to be a residential component. The restaurant is also a
26   challenge based on the square footage and the parking that is required for that square footage.
27
28   Mr. Laughlin noted that the power lines make this property very difficult to develop in a practical
29   manner. Moving the building as close to Highland Drive as possible is what he would like to see.
30   There will not be an eyesore created and there will not be a three-story wall. It will be an
31   architecturally designed building that has some visual interest. He thanked Ms. Marsh and Mr.
32   Teerlink for their efforts related to this site. This is a plan that meets the requirements and makes
33   financial sense. Mr. Laughlin stated that he needs approval at the current meeting to move forward.
34
35   Chair Roach noted that City Staff has mentioned a Condition of Approval to move the building 10
36   feet back so it is not right against the sidewalk. He asked if that was something that would be possible.
37   Mr. Laughlin explained that it would be challenging. If that is not a requirement for the zone, he
38   would rather it be as close as possible. It might be possible to add in some trees or landscaping, but
39   he is not sure how far out the building can be. There were no additional Commissioner questions.
40
41   Chair Roach opened the public hearing.
42
43   Sarah Pearce gave her address as 2004 Arbor Lane and explained that she is an immediate neighbor
44   of the proposed development. She is supportive of the project with the conditions outlined. Having
45   the extra trees on the site will be beneficial as will the graduated height near the residential areas.
46

     City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting – 04/15/2025

                                                         4
 1   Steve Glaser lives at 2052 East Arbor Lane and is supportive of the proposal. He asked about the For
 2   Sale sign that is currently on the property. He wanted to know if there had been a change in the plans.
 3
 4   Mike Shuping lives at 1945 East Vintage Woods Court and expressed support for the project.
 5
 6   Chris Layton gave his address as 3200 East 3900 South and explained that he is the architect on this
 7   project. As a previous Commissioner, he understands how difficult these types of decisions can be.
 8   There are certain challenges when it comes to the uses that are in demand and the uses that are needed.
 9   It is important to work with property owners who want to develop projects that add value to the
10   community. He feels this proposal will add value to the City. Both a restaurant space and office
11   space are vital and will work well in this location. Additional residences are also needed in the
12   community. He hopes that all of this will be taken into consideration during the deliberations.
13
14   There were no further comments. The public hearing was closed.
15
16   The applicant was invited to address comments from the public hearing. Mr. Laughlin explained that
17   there was a point where the project was not feasible, so he had no choice but to try to sell. However,
18   if this application moves forward, he has everything lined up to move forward with what is proposed.
19   City Attorney, Brad Christopherson, reminded the Commission that for a motion to be successful, the
20   vote would need to be unanimous. Four votes are needed to pass a motion.
21
22   Commissioner Karianne Prince likes what has been proposed and is inclined to support the project,
23   as modified. She understands some of the suggestions but pointed out that the applicant needs to
24   navigate the power lines. While she likes the idea of a bigger sidewalk and buffer, she is not sure that
25   she is willing to support a Condition of Approval related to the size. Chair Roach believed one of the
26   original plans for the site showed the building further back. He asked how the conflict with the power
27   lines was handled at that time. Mr. Teerlink explained that it was on the other side of the easement.
28   It was located where the four townhome units have since been added. Ms. Marsh reported that in the
29   C-2 Zone, even within residential uses, there could be some commercial uses in those townhomes.
30   For instance, those could be designed in a way where there is office space on the main floor. That
31   kind of use could increase some of the commercial on the overall site. Some examples of commercial
32   uses that could work there include beauty services, personal services, and offices.
33
34   Commissioner Fonte expressed appreciation for the image that was shared for reference. She
35   encouraged the applicant to focus on landscaping as much as possible. While she understands there
36   is a need for housing and commercial space, she feels a row of trees or bushes along Highland Drive
37   would be beneficial. She does not want to see Holladay looking like other nearby communities.
38   Holladay has more vegetation and that is something that differentiates it from many other cities.
39   Commissioner Fonte is inclined to approve the application but stressed the need for landscaping.
40
41   Commissioner Cunningham noted that the Staff Report states: “Multi-family development is a
42   permitted use when it is accessory to a permitted or conditional use.” There are less than 10,000
43   square feet of commercial listed. He asked if that meets the code requirement that the use be
44   accessory. Mr. Teerlink explained that there have been past discussions about the appropriate ratio.
45   Applicants are typically told that commercial is first and the accessory uses come after, but the
46   Planning Commission can decide whether the mix is acceptable for the zone. There is no clear

     City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting – 04/15/2025

                                                        5
 1   guidance in the ordinance itself about what the ratio is. Ms. Marsh clarified that the 10,000 square
 2   feet listed is the minimum land area required per use. The residential use is 10,000 square feet plus
 3   2,000 for each unit. That tabulation ends up being 34,000 square feet of land required for what the
 4   applicant is proposing and there is 49,000 square feet of land. The Staff Report looks at whether the
 5   minimums are met. Mr. Teerlink shared information about the 10-foot-wide sidewalk and the setback
 6   off of that sidewalk.
 7
 8   Commissioner Cunningham referenced the Staff recommendations that have been made. He asked
 9   how strongly Staff wants the Planning Commission to consider those. Mr. Teerlink reported that the
10   recommendation creates buffering and an area for landscaping. It is a good starting point.
11   Commissioner Cunningham is a little bit troubled by the applicant's request to make a decision at the
12   current Planning Commission Meeting. There are four Commissioners present and he would prefer
13   the full Commission to consider the application. He is also struggling with the 10-foot setback, as
14   Staff has made solid arguments for that. Mr. Teerlink believes the Commission might feel more
15   comfortable if the Final Site Plan and Final Subdivision came back with all of those details.
16
17   Chair Roach likes what has been proposed because the neighbors feel good about it and it makes
18   sense for the applicant. However, he has concerns about the landscaping. He reminded those present
19   that Holladay is part of Tree City USA. With the building all the way against the sidewalk, he sees
20   some potential conflicts but also wants to be sensitive to the needs of the applicant. He asked if it
21   would be possible to incorporate some tree cutouts. Mr. Laughlin confirmed that this is possible and
22   reminded Commissioners that he is a resident of Holladay rather than a developer. Chair Roach
23   wondered what kind of condition could be included in the motion language to mitigate the 10-foot
24   clearance zone but still accommodate the need for landscaping and trees. Ms. Marsh noted that there
25   could be an average setback of five feet across with a certain amount of trees placed in the area. There
26   are average setbacks for residential and other uses so there can be variation in the architecture.
27
28   Commissioner Cunningham would prefer to require the 10 feet and then consider adjustment later.
29   He feels a lot has been given away on this project already. Commissioner Prince is not certain that
30   anything has been lost. She understands his comments but wants to see something positive happen
31   on this property. Rather than delegating the Final Plat back to Staff, it could come to the Planning
32   Commission for review. Commissioner Cunningham expressed support for it coming back to the
33   Planning Commission. He suggested starting with a 10-foot setback. The Commission discussed the
34   setbacks. Ms. Marsh reiterated the option for an average setback rather than a 10-foot setback.
35
36   Additional discussions were had about setbacks. Ms. Marsh acknowledged that there are challenges
37   on the site due to the power lines. Moving the building 10 feet into the parking lot area could impact
38   the number of available parking stalls. That could create parking issues. If 10 feet are taken off of
39   the size of the building itself, then the amount of commercial space would be reduced. Chair Roach
40   mentioned the dining patio on the south side of the building. He asked if that is considered
41   commercial space. Ms. Marsh stated that it is not part of the building, but restaurants will use that in
42   their table calculations for seating. Commissioner Fonte asked if the decks could be made smaller.
43   Mr. Laughlin explained that the restaurant portion needs to be a certain size. Chair Roach noted that
44   the Planning Commission is trying to consider options that work best for all parties involved while
45   still meeting the criteria. Commissioner Fonte does not like that the applicant needs a decision to be


     City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting – 04/15/2025

                                                        6
 1   made at the current Planning Commission Meeting. Commissioner Cunningham believes that if the
 2   vote is taken at the current meeting, then the 10-foot recommendation from Staff should be included.
 3
 4   Mr. Laughlin informed Commissioners that if a decision is not made at the current Planning
 5   Commission Meeting, then the For Sale sign has to remain. He needs to be able to move the
 6   residential element forward. Mr. Laughlin explained that he purchased the property to address an
 7   eyesore that was in the community. He is not a developer and this has been a very expensive process.
 8   If there is approval received from the Planning Commission, there will continue to be collaboration
 9   on the details. If it is possible to add in some landscaping, then he will make sure that happens.
10
11   Chair Roach asked about the possibility of approving the application with a Condition of Approval
12   for the 10-foot setback. The applicant could then come back with the final details. He wanted to
13   know if that would be a better scenario than continuing the application until the next meeting. Mr.
14   Laughlin confirmed that it would be better than a continuation, as he needs those involved with the
15   project to make certain commitments. Otherwise, it is not possible for this to move forward.
16
17   Discussions were had about comparable Site Plans, such as the office building to the south of the
18   subject property. Chair Roach believed the question is whether the Planning Commission will use
19   the Staff recommendation for the motion language or make a motion to continue the item. There was
20   support expressed by the Commissioners to follow the Staff recommendation in the Staff Report. Ms.
21   Marsh reminded Commissioners that there will need to be two motions made for this item. One
22   element of the Subdivision motion is a recommendation to the City Council to vacate a portion of
23   Arbor Lane. That is noted in the recommended language in the Meeting Materials Packet.
24
25   Commissioner Prince moved to APPROVE the Preliminary Plat for “5025 South Highland Drive,”
26   a Mixed-Use Planned Unit Development in the C-2 Zone, based upon the following:
27
28   Findings:
29
30          1.      The Preliminary Plat has been reviewed and considered substantially complete.
31
32          2.      Development proposals, as provided, remain in accordance with the Development
33                  Agreement approved by the City Council.

     City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting – 04/15/2025

                                                         8
 1   CONTINUED HEARING ITEMS
 2   2.  Continued - Text Amendment - Chapter 13.84 - Outdoor Lighting Standards.
 3       Continued Review of Proposed Amendments to Title 13 of the Holladay City Code, Land
 4       Use and Development Regulations. By Order of the Holladay City Council, the Proposal
 5       Relocates Current Lighting Standards from Various Sections of Title 13 and
 6       Consolidates them within a New and Expanded City Outdoor Lighting Section Proposed
 7       as Holladay Ordinance §13.84. The Item is Reviewed as a Legislative Action, According
 8       to Procedures Outlined in the Holladay Ordinance §13.07. File #25-4-02.
 9
10   Mr. Teerlink presented the Staff Report and explained that this is a Text Amendment for Chapter
11   13.84 – Outdoor Lighting Standards. Staff has prepared changes based on previous Commissioner
12   comments. Mr. Teerlink reported that he received a text message from Council Member Emily Gray.
13   Council Member Gray received a comment from someone unable to attend the meeting. That
14   comment was forwarded to the Commissioners and can be read aloud and entered into the record.
15
16   Chair Roach opened the public hearing.
17
18   An email from Andy White was read into the record. Mr. White explained that he was out of State
19   and asked that his comments be forwarded to the Planning Commission. He has concerns about
20   residential lighting. Holladay is known for having neighborly citizens who participate in local events
21   but is also known for having quiet tree-lined streets. There is little an individual can do to prevent
22   house lights or yard boundary lights from turning a pleasant evening stroll into something intrusive.
23
24   Kim Duffy gave her address as 2195 Walker Lane. Two nearby houses have very bright lights on
25   them. She shared information about the homes and the intense lights. Ms. Duffy previously wrote
26   those homeowners a letter about the lanterns. This is becoming a problem and she does not feel there
27   should be bright lights on houses. Mr. White drove around the City to see how most houses in the
28   City were lit. Most had two or three lights, which included a porch light and a garage light. However,
29   that is not the case in her area, as intense lights are being installed on certain homes. Ms. Duffy
30   expressed support for an ordinance that will address lighting issues moving forward.
31
32   There were no further comments. The public hearing was closed.
33
34   During the Work Session, the Planning Commission discussed the proposed Text Amendment.
35   Mr. Teerlink made notes during the Work Session. Whenever an amendment is being recommended
36   by the Planning Commission to the City Council, it is beneficial for all members of the Planning
37   Commission to make their voices heard during the vote. Since there are four Commissioners present
38   at the current meeting, it might make sense to continue the Text Amendment to the next meeting.
39
40   Commissioner Fonte wanted to know what could be done to address the issues mentioned during the
41   public hearing. She asked what residents can do when there are lighting concerns. Mr. Teerlink
42   explained that whenever a new law is established, there can be legal non-conforming situations
43   created. There was a discussion with the City Council about a requirement that within 180 days, non-
44   compliant lighting would have to come into compliance, but there was no support for that suggestion.
45   He noted that there is a Code Enforcement Officer who has dealt with light issues from time to time.
46
